primary_record.title: Diverse beam search to find densest-known planar unit distance graphs
primary_record.reported_search_scope: Moser-lattice diverse backtracking beam search, with a database of about sixty million discovered graphs
primary_record.provenance_note: The paper describes classical GPU beam search. Section 6.1 mentions AI only as a possible future use of the graph database; it does not report generative-AI assistance in the search that produced Table 2.

authors_repository.readme_description: Code for the published beam search. Its README links the Moser-coordinate graph database through a Figshare sharing URL.

database_access.status: not downloaded; browser access returned HTTP 403 and direct access was met with a WAF challenge
database_access.effect: The n=100 439-point-list witness is not reproduced here. The reported value remains a source claim and is kept separate from the reproduced 261 human baseline.

current_frontier_check.finding: The survey cites 439 as the largest reported value for real-plane n=100 from arXiv:2406.15317v3, reports exact values through n=21 from arXiv:2412.11914v2, and notes that arXiv:2606.29415v2 publishes no n=100 comparison table. The latter paper reports AI code-assistant use for code optimization, but gives no competing 100-point result.
current_frontier_check.optimality: open; no upper-bound proof for u(100) matching 439 was found in the checked sources
